whatItIs.text: A cabbage-family vegetable grown for its dark green flowering head and thick stalk; its flavour compounds survive steaming and stir-frying better than boiling.

historyNote.text: Broccoli was bred from Mediterranean cabbage landraces from about the sixth century BC and refined in Roman Italy — the name is Italian for the flowering crest of a cabbage — and reached North America with Italian immigrants in the 19th century.

howToChoose.text: Choose heads with tight, dark green florets and firm stalks; yellowing buds mean it is about to flower and turn bitter.

storage.text: Keep loosely wrapped in the fridge and use while the florets are still tight.

useItUp.text: The peeled stalk is the sweetest part; tired florets go into soup or fried rice.

substitutions.note: milder and creamier when cooked, same roasting behaviour
